articleTitle: A Novel Single-Switch High Step-Up DC-DC Converter Based on Quadratic Boost for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The resiliency of the power grid can be further improved by decentralized power generation from various renewable energy resources. High step-up DC-DC converters find extensive use in such applications, including solar photovoltaic (PV) arrays, LED lighting, UPS, and fuel cells, as well as providing sufficient voltage levels to feed grid-connected inverters. The present paper proposes a new structure for a high step-up DC-DC converter employing a single-switch arrangement, addressing the urgent demand for high-voltage gain power solutions. The converter, distinguished by its costeffective utilization of widely available components and a single low-side main switch, along with lower buffer capacitor voltage stress and identical uncoupled inductors, results in a compact design. Furthermore, the continuous input current characteristic fulfills the requirements of renewable energy applications. With proven applications in diverse fields, the proposed structure addresses the necessity for high voltage ratio DC-DC converters, facilitating the transformation of low voltage to significantly higher voltages to feed inverters or any DC bus system. Additionally, the paper provides detailed formulas, operational states, and simulation results using MATLAB/Simulink, validating the efficacy of the proposed converter.

articleTitle: A Review on Machine Learning Model Implementation for Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This review study aims to identify the main research trends in the implementation of machine learning algorithms to model and study issues related to photovoltaic systems. This study mainly focuses on research papers published lately in 2023 revealing the main trends of implantation of machine learning algorithms in the literature. The outputs of this study could provide insights into the current status of machine learning model potentials to improve photovoltaic systems performances.

articleTitle: Flexible Microgrid Scheduling with the Presence of Renewable Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The growing need for energy has led to the high installation of renewable energy resources (RES), especially wind turbines (WT) and photovoltaic (PV). Although these generations provide cheap power to the power grid, the uncertainty of their output power, along with other uncertainties of the power system, such as demands, leads to imbalances in the power system. The system operator requires a flexible energy portfolio of various distributed energy resources (DER) to cope with uncertainties and reduce imbalances. This study proposes a flexible optimal scheduling model for microgrid (MG) participation in the electricity market. Various DERs, including WT, PV, conventional generators (CG), and battery energy storage systems (BESS), are considered. Also, dynamic line rating (DLR) equipment is installed on the line connected to the upstream network. The simulation is implemented on the standard 33-busses IEEE. The flexibility indices (FI) for the line with DLR equipment and the CG are calculated to show the effect of DLR on flexibility. Then, the total system’s flexibility index (SFI) is calculated by the provided weights and used to compare in different case studies, i.e., static line rating (SLR) and DLR models. Finally, the effect of RES penetration increments on the net profit of MG, total energy sold and purchased, unit flexibility, and the SFI are compared. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model in improving net profit and the SFI.

articleTitle: Bidirectional LLC-DAB Converter for Battery Charger Applications: Analysis and Design
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: abstract-Efficient and reliable energy conversion in power electronics converters is intricately linked to the implementation of soft switching, a key factor offering heightened efficiency, lower Electromagnetic Interference (EMI), increased power density, and prevention of overheating issues. Using LLC and DAB soft-switching converters in conjunction, the paper explores the synergistic potential of using both technologies while mitigating their inherent weaknesses. The proposed methodology involves incorporating LLC for light load conditions, providing voltage regulation capabilities, and seamlessly transitioning to DAB for heavier loads. The viability of this approach is substantiated through simulation using MATLAB/Simulink, offering insights into its performance across diverse load ranges.

articleTitle: Optimal Fuzzy-Based Controller for DVR to Improve Power Quality Considering Various Fault Types
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Currently, maintaining power quality (PQ) poses a fundamental challenge in power systems. Voltage disturbances such as voltage swell, voltage sag, various fault types, harmonics, and the high penetration of power electronic-based loads into the power grid lead to a decline in power quality. Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR) is an effective solution for mitigating voltage disturbances and harmonic distortions in various fault types conditions, and non-linear loads of power systems. In this research, a dynamic voltage restorer system based on an optimal fuzzy controller, utilizing the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) approach is proposed to enhance power quality in power systems. Additionally, the proposed technique is compared to a Fuzzy-PI controller to maintain load voltage within acceptable levels and reduce the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) arising from power electronic components. The results demonstrate that the proposed control method significantly reduces the total harmonic deviation of load voltage and improves DVR performance compared to the Fuzzy-PI controller. Ultimately, the effectiveness of the results is confirmed through MATLAB/SIMULINK simulation analysis.

articleTitle: Flexibility Assessment of Virtual Power Plant with Considering Dispatchable Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Nowadays, the uncertainty in the power system parameters has led to more operator flexibility requirements. Flexibility is the system’s capability to manage uncertainties and balance the supply-load equilibrium. This study presents an optimal operation model of distributed generation resources to supply electrical and thermal load as a virtual power plant for participating in the electricity market. Normalized up-ward and down-ward flexibility indices (FI) are expressed for demand response programs, conventional generators, and energy storage systems. Additionally, by assigning weights to each of the above indices, the up-ward and down-ward FI of the whole system has been calculated. The model has been evaluated on the standard 33-busses IEEE distribution system. The results show that the suggested flexibility model accurately quantifies the flexibility of the system, giving the system operator an adequate view of the system’s hourly flexibility.

articleTitle: Investigating Role of Renewable Resources Including Wind Turbines in Energy Hub by Considering Simultaneous Demand for Electricity, Heating and Cooling
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: As a crucial component of multi-energy systems (MES), the energy hub significantly enhances their performance and reliability. In the energy system, the utilization of renewable energy sources (RES) can presents a significant optimization problem, capable of substantially reducing environmental pollution and lowering energy costs for users. This paper presents an optimal load dispatch model incorporating a collection of wind turbines, aimed at reducing the overall cost of operating an energy hub. It is also proposes a hub structure based on wind, natural gas, and electricity as a combined heat and power system, utilizing converters and energy storage mechanisms to obtain electricity, thermal, and cooling energy. To accomplish this, two situations are executed in the network, aiming to minimize costs by applying a problem-solving approach to the installation of wind turbines at an energy hub. After implementing energy hub management in the optimal mode, the system’s operating costs are reduced by $16 \%$, demonstrating its advantage.

articleTitle: Optimal Coordination of Directional Overcurrent Relays for Fuse Saving in Distribution Networks With Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Ensuring the fuse remains intact during a fault is a key challenge in coordinating protection devices within distribution networks and microgrids. Coordinating protection becomes more complicated with the integration of distributed generations and different operating modes. To address the issue of undetected faults by the recloser in island mode, employing a pair of directional over-current relays on the lines could be a viable solution. Similarly, the fault current limiter is used to apply consistent settings for relay characteristics in various operating modes of the distribution network. In this paper, we want to optimize the value of fault current limiter and relays settings be set in such a way which the total operation time of the main and backup relays is minimized and the coordination between relay-relay and relay-fuse is maintained. To achieve this, genetic algorithm has been used to calculate the optimal value of relay settings and fault current limiter. The advantage of this design is avoiding mistakes in protection zones due to resistance or measurement errors. Moreover, eliminating the need for telecommunication system, and requiring single settings for relays compared to similar approaches is other remarkable advancement in this method.

articleTitle: A Novel Single-Switch Self-balanced Bipolar Step-Up DC–DC Converter Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents a novel high voltage gain boost converter with bipolar outputs. The output ports of the converter share a common ground with the input source. Direct connection of the input source to the neutral point of AC and bipolar DC grids eliminates common mode leakage currents. The proposed topology ensures continuous input current and utilizes only a single switch. Moreover, the converter has self-balancing ability in the output capacitors. These features make it a promising choice for bipolar DC microgrid applications and as an input source for inverters like the single-phase half-bridge inverter. Employing coupled inductors in the converter reduces component count and the total price. Furthermore, the maximum voltage stress on the switch and diodes is equal to half of the total output voltage, providing an additional advantage for bipolar output converters. The paper includes a theoretical analysis and a comparative study with other bipolar converters. Finally, to verify the analysis, simulation results based on MATLAB Simulink are presented.

articleTitle: An Interleaved boost converter for connecting distributed generation sources to Bipolar DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel high step-up converter based on Interleaved Boost structure with two symmetrical outputs, which makes it suitable for bipolar DC microgrid (BPDCMG) applications. The structure eliminates problems associated with the unbalancing of BPDCMG and prevents flow of leakage currents through the grid. The proposed converter has continuous input current with low ripple and has a common ground with output’s neutral point makes it suitable for BPDCMG. In this paper, the proposed converter is discussed and a 640 W prototype of the proposed converter is simulated in balanced an unbalanced situations to verify the operation of the structure.

articleTitle: Simulation of wind flow effect on the cooling of solar panels (in Tehran)
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Solar energy is one of the most favorable renewable energy sources, so investigating the factors affecting the efficiency of solar panels is important. In this paper, the effect of natural wind flow on the cooling of solar panels in the region is studied. Three conditions without wind, wind at a speed of 5 m.s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, and wind at a speed of 10 m.s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> are simulated using PVsyst software. The effect of cooling on the power output, performance ratio, return on investment, and carbon emissions prevention of solar panels is explored in this paper. According to the results obtained from the simulation, heat loss at maximum wind speed is 9% less than when there is no wind flow.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Impact of External Interventions on Water and Energy Demand: Cybersecurity’s Role in Sustainable Development
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The nexus of water, food, and energy constitutes a fundamental aspect of sustainable development. Furthermore, the demand for water and energy is becoming more pronounced. Moreover, there is a growing importance placed on studying cyber security within the water-energy nexus. This research investigates the interdependence of these two systems, conceptualizing them as a water-energy nexus and effort has been conducted on optimizing the economic efficiency of electricity and water systems in order to minimize operating expenses. Subsequently, external interventions, such as the simultaneous injection of false data on both water and energy demand, were addressed through an optimization process in GAMS software. The results suggest that the value of the cost objective function remains constant when inaccurate data is introduced, which hinders the accurate estimation of the system by the system operator. in this system, both water and power loads are directly impacted by these interventions. In particular, the power and water load of the system have exhibited changes ranging from 1.5% to 17.99% for electric load and 3.87% to 17.1% for water load, in comparison to the previous state.

articleTitle: Curtailment Reduction of Renewable Generations Through Power-to-Hydrogen Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: With the worldwide increasing penetration of renewable power generations, their curtailment rate has also increased owing to several reasons including the lack of transmission capacity, grid congestion limits, and surplus generation during low load hours. Green hydrogen and Power-to-Hydrogen (PtH) units play an important role in the reduction of renewable power curtailments as well as the reduction of power grid total costs. It is the purpose of this paper to investigate the reduction of renewable generation curtailments via employment of PtH units. Candidate wind farms and PtH units are applied to the modified IEEE 24-bus power system in a 15-year planning scope with an annual load rise of $\% 2$. The MILP problem is solved in GAMS software via Gurobi solver and four cases are taken into account based on the hydrogen bid variations and the curtailment penalty changes. It is observed that without utilizing PtH units, there are large amounts of wind power curtailments. However, in the presence of PtH units, the annual curtailments are decreased significantly. Moreover, both the hydrogen bid as well as the curtailment penalty effect the curtailment reduction of renewable-based generations. The higher the hydrogen bids and curtailment penalties, the more the curtailment reductions.

articleTitle: Self-Assembled Monolayer-based Hole Transporting Materials for Invert Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The escalating global energy consumption is predominantly attributed to the burgeoning population growth, resulting in increased demand for energy resources; hence, the imperative to shift towards sustainable energy sources is emphasized. In this context, solar energy appears particularly promising due to its abundant, clean, and renewable characteristics. One significant aspect of solar cells is hole transport materials (HTMs), where we are currently witnessing a revolution in hole transport materials based on self-assembled monolayers (SAM-HTMs); this category of materials has significantly contributed to notable enhancements in power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) in inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Despite the fabrication of the first SAM-based PSC occurring in late 2018, SAM-HTMs have emerged as a promising alternative such as PTAA, primarily due to various advantages such, as tunable bandgap, robust interface stability, and easy fabrication. This class of materials holds the potential to advance the energy sector and expedite the rapid industrialization of PSCs.

articleTitle: Integrating Photovoltaic Systems into Urban Infrastructure: A Case Study of Tehran International Tower
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In recent years, the integration of photovoltaic solar energy solutions into building structures has garnered significant attention. However, the implementation of photovoltaic systems in existing buildings presents various challenges. This study aims to evaluate the performance of a photovoltaic system integrated with a building in Tehran. The residential Tehran International Tower was chosen as the subject of the study, and the DesignBuilder and PV system software were utilized for the design and assessment of the integrated photovoltaic system. The study investigated the energy output of the photovoltaic system and its impact on reducing CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. The findings revealed that the installation of photovoltaic panels on the facade and windows of Tehran International Tower could generate a total of 1946 megawatt hours of energy annually. This energy production would be sufficient to fully power the building’s lighting department, with an additional surplus production of 198,045 kilowatt hours per year. Furthermore, it was determined that this solar energy production could prevent the release of 3167.97 tons of carbon dioxide annually.

articleTitle: A Modified Quadratic Boost Converter with Continuous Input Current for PV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This study presents a high-gain quadratic DC-DC converter designed to deliver substantial voltage amplification. Eliminating the transformer and having a common ground between input and output has resulted in a smaller size and increased versatility. Furthermore, the converter has a continuous input current, making it suitable for PV applications. The paper develops equations to describe the converter, compares ideal and non-ideal conditions, and investigates non-ideal voltage gain, losses, and efficiency. Simulations are run to validate the derived equations, and the findings are presented.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Current Control Of Asymmetrical Six-phase Induction Machine-based Integrated Onboard Charger in EVs
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Integrated on-board chargers (IOBC) have gained attention due to their advantages in reducing costs, size, and weight of electrical vehicle (EV). The crucial challenge in IOBC is to achieve zero torque in order to eliminate mechanical interlocking. This article proposes a finite-time sliding mode current control approach for a six-phase induction machinebased integrated on-board charger (IOBC). First-order sliding mode controller used for stator phases current control. The sliding mode control aims to suppress estimation errors and ensure finite-time convergence of the stator currents to their desired references. To nullify machine torque production during the charging mode and achieve a balanced three-phase grid current, the sequence of stator currents is adjusted to maintain balanced xy currents simultaneously. Both the $\alpha \beta$ and $0+0$ - currents are also controlled to zero. The results are validated by MATLAB Simulink and show that the proposed control has good performance in eliminating torque and accurately tracking current.

articleTitle: A Quadratic Based High Voltage Gain Converter Using Coupled Inductors and Switched Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this article, an ultra-high step-up quadratic converter with continuous input current is proposed. Using the coupled inductors and switch capacitors, the converter voltage gain is improved significantly. This converter adds no switch and magnetic core to the basic quadratic structure. A passive clamp circuit absorbs the leakage inductance energy of the coupled inductor and recycles to the output. Also, the reverse recovery issue of most diodes is solved. Furthermore, the converter enjoys from common ground. The presented structure operation and analysis are presented, and the converter is simulated in PSpice software. Loss breakdown analysis is performed which shows 95.3% efficiency at 200 W. Also, to show the converter advantages, this converter is compared with several counterparts.

articleTitle: Electrical Load Consumption and Photovoltaic Power Forecasting using Deep CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The modern world is highly dependent on electricity and needs a continuous supply of load demand. During the past decades, renewable energies (REs), as clean and economical sources, have been developed to answer the increasing load demand. However, both renewable energy production and electricity consumption have random characteristics caused by different uncertain factors such as weather conditions and customer behavior. Therefore, it is crucial to simultaneously perform load forecasting and RE generation prediction in areas where most of the demand is supplied by REs. This study proposes a forecasting framework based on a deep three-dimensional convolutional neural network for load forecasting and photovoltaic (PV) power prediction. In this way, power system operators can balance demand and supply based on the predicted values. Also, using the same framework, which is capable of forecasting both load and PV power, would significantly reduce computational costs. The comparative analysis for 15-min, 90-min, 3-h, and 6-h ahead horizon shows that the accuracy of the proposed method increased in all time horizons compared to long short-term memory (LSTM), gated recurrent unit (GRU), and two-dimensional convolutional neural network (Conv2D).

articleTitle: Optimal Resilient Operation of Multi-Carrier Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper proposes a resilient operational scheduling model for Multi-Carrier Energy Systems (MCESs) that operate in various time horizons and energy markets. This model considers electrical, cooling, and heating energy markets as well as multiple distributed energy resources. The proposed model optimizes the MCES’s operation by minimizing operation costs in the day-ahead market (DAM), reducing the deviation between the day-ahead and real-time (RTM) markets, and minimizing interruption costs and mismatches in operation costs in RTM. The model also includes preventive actions for external shocks and corrective actions to manage the outage zones effectively. When evaluated on a modified 123-bus MCES, the proposed model demonstrated a 20% decrease in expected costs in comparison to the base case. This study contributes to the field of energy markets by proposing a three-stage optimization model as well as using preventive and corrective actions to optimize the operation of MCESs.

articleTitle: Perylene Diimide Molecules as Acceptor Materials in Organic Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In recent years, non-fullerene acceptor materials have garnered significant attention and utilization in organic solar cells (OSCs) devices, primarily owing to their favorable optical properties and the ease of tuning their electronic energy levels through synthetic methods. The utilization of non-fullerene acceptors represents a prominent focal point in the ongoing research and development of bulk-heterojunction OSCs. Notably, recent advancements in this area have led to remarkable enhancements in power conversion efficiency (PCE), with PCE levels surpassing the $20 \%$ threshold. Perylene diimide (PDI), a prominent example of a non-fullerene acceptor material, has emerged as a subject of extensive investigation due to its favorable attributes such as high electron affinity and excellent charge transport properties. Its widespread study stems from its capacity for efficient light transmission and electron capture. Through an in-depth examination, the article elucidates the impact of PDI-based acceptor materials on OSC device efficiency and outlines the evolving landscape of their application in renewable energy technologies.

articleTitle: Regional Wind Power Forecasting Based on CNNBiLSTM-ReliefF Method
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The noisy and stochastic nature of wind power production introduces many challenges to the grid. Wind power forecasting methods can effectively predict these uncertainties and ensure the stable operation of power systems. Due to the superior performance of deep learning approaches in predicting nonlinear data, a hybrid method based on two-dimensional convolutional neural network (Conv2D), bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM), and ReliefF algorithm is presented in this study. First, wind power data are preprocessed. Then, the processed data are entered into each Conv2D and BiLSTM network for temporal-spatial feature extraction. Finally, the features that are extracted from these two networks are combined by assigning weights to them through the ReliefF algorithm for final wind power prediction. The forecasting performance of the presented method is tested on a real aggregated dataset of Belgium for 15 minutes ahead regional wind power forecasting. According to the results, the proposed model has higher accuracy than long short-term memory, gated recurrent unit (GRU), BiLSTM, and Conv2D networks.

articleTitle: Modeling and Controller Design for a GaN-based AC-DC LED Driver
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents the modeling and controller design for an AC/DC LED driver using Gallium Nitride (GaN) switching semiconductors. The proposed configuration integrates a full-bridge rectifier with a de/dc Sepic converter. Firstly, the detailed modeling of the Sepic converter in discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) is presented. To facilitate the small-signal modeling process, the PWM averaging method is employed. A closed-loop controller is then implemented to ensure system stability. To establish a baseline for comparison, the controller parameters are tuned manually and via the Genetic Algorithm (GA). Simulation results confirm the accuracy of the modeling and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed controller design framework. Finally, the GaN switch is replaced by Silicon Carbide (SiC) and conventional Silicon (Si) to assess the driver efficiency. Simulation in the PLECS environment highlight the high efficiency of GaN switch and lower heat generation compared to SiC and Si, reducing the need for extensive cooling and potentially extending the converter’s lifespan.

articleTitle: Improvement of DC Power Response Using Artificial Neural Network in an Off-Grid PV System Linked to a Constant Power Load
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: With the growth of renewable energies, solar electricity is applied to power various loads like electric motors and illuminants, researchers conduct extensive studies on achieving electricity production with high power quality. The output power from the photovoltaic system undergoes considerable variability, necessitating the use of maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithms. In this article, the traditional P&O controller and the intelligent fuzzy logic (FL) controller are initially examined. Subsequently, a fast and reliable artificial neural network (FR-ANN) controller is formulated, designed to perform effectively under conditions of irradiation and variable temperature by assimilating favorable attributes from other controllers through learning. The photovoltaic system is simulated in the MATLAB/Simulink environment and provides power to a constant power load sensitive to voltage drop. Through the application of the FRANN controller, an improvement in system stability is observed in the event of a voltage drop.

articleTitle: A Novel Tri-State High Step-Up DC-DC Converter With Coupled Inductor
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In this article, a tri-state DC-DC converter is presented, which employs a coupled inductor. The converter proposed herein features a simple design, high voltage gain, minimized voltage stress on switches and diodes, consistent output current, and a shared ground. The mathematical analysis takes into account several factors, including the continuous conduction mode (CCM) of the proposed converters, the voltage stress experienced by semiconductor devices, and the design aspects of components. Following the comparison with various converters mentioned in other references, the results are discussed. Additionally, simulation results of the proposed converter are presented at a power level of 500 watts, using PLECS software, to validate the theoretical arguments put forth in the article.

articleTitle: A New Topology For High Gain DC DC Converter Using Coupled Inductor
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper presents a novel step-up DC/DC converter that incorporates an active switch and a coupled inductor. The utilization of a coupled inductor and an active switched inductor enables the proposed converter to attain a noteworthy efficiency and voltage conversion ratio while keeping an appropriate duty cycle. Furthermore, this design efficiently alleviates the voltage stresses placed on the power switches. As a result, it facilitates the utilization of lowresistance devices and minimizes conduction losses, ultimately leading to improved overall efficiency. This article elaborates on the steady-state analysis and operational principles of the proposed topology. In order to check the benefits of the provided converter, the topology has been compared with previous high gain converters. Finally, in order to validate the provided theoretical analysis, the provided converter was simulated in PLECS software and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Optimizing Renewable Microgrids for Green Hydrogen in Industrial Settings: A Case Study in the Steel Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The steel industry is under mounting pressure to minimize its carbon emissions and shift towards sustainable energy sources. This research explores the potential of integrating renewable microgrids to facilitate green hydrogen production for use in steel manufacturing processes. The study offers a comprehensive examination of the technical, economic, and environmental aspects of this integration, shedding light on the advantages and obstacles linked to the adoption of green hydrogen technology in industrial settings. HOMER Pro software was employed to model the systems under investigation. The findings indicate that the PV/WT/Grid/EL system makes green hydrogen production feasible for industrial consumers, with hydrogen and electric energy production costs of $33.8 \$ / \mathrm{kg}$ and $0.012 \$ / \mathrm{kWh}$, respectively. Furthermore, the PV/Grid/EL system emerges as the most optimal choice in terms of greenhouse gas emissions.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Microgrid Configurations for Sustainable Energy Supply in Kish Island
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Despite the intermittent nature of renewable energy sources, which can pose challenges to grid sustainability, nuclear power has traditionally been a significant supplier of clean energy, albeit with limited flexibility. However, recent technological advances have led to the development of scaled-down iterations of large nuclear power plants that offer greater flexibility while still ensuring clean and stable electricity delivery. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of a microgrid configuration designed for Kish Island. It focuses on integrating micro-modular reactors (MMR), wind turbines, photovoltaic (PV) panels, and lithium-ion battery storage. The objective of this study is to optimize energy production and storage in a microgrid, enabling sustainable electricity supply in Kish Island, Iran. The economic implications of two microgrid configurations are evaluated. The first configuration includes 8 MMRs and a battery, while the second configuration includes PV, wind turbines, 4 MMRs, and a battery. These configurations are assessed based on two key metrics: net present cost (NPC) and levelized cost of energy (LCOE). The results indicate that the PV/Wind/4 MMRs/Battery configuration reduces NPC and LCOE by 47.1% and 59.1%, respectively, underscoring its economic advantage for Kish Island. By incorporating renewable energy sources such as PV and wind turbines alongside nuclear power, the microgrid can provide a more sustainable and cost-effective electricity supply for the island. This underscores the potential of integrating different energy sources to enhance grid flexibility and efficiency.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Number of blocks on PEM Fuel-cell Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This research paper delves into the analysis and comparison of two distinct geometries that can be employed to accommodate blocks in the oxygen channel. A fuel cell is an apparatus that generates electricity through the chemical reaction between hydrogen and oxygen, and this form of energy has garnered significant interest from scientists due to its eco-friendliness. The research team discovered that blocks can be strategically placed in the path of oxygen flow within a fuel cell to enhance its performance. By directing the oxygen fluid towards the membrane and gas diffusion layers, the contact surface between the hydrogen and oxygen fluids is augmented. The computational fluid dynamics technique was utilized to evaluate the efficacy of these channels. This approach relies on predicting fluid behavior by solving equations governing them using a computer. The study outlines the modeling and analysis stages of these channels. The team designed blocks in two different quantities, namely three blocks and ten blocks, with each block being triangular in shape.

articleTitle: High Step-up Quadratic Converter With ZVS Operation and Continuous Input Current
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper proposed a high step-up converter based on the quadratic structure with soft switching operation. In this converter, high voltage gain is obtained by the coupled inductors which also, can control the switch voltage stress. A ZVT circuit provides ZVZCS condition at turn-on for the main switch and absorbs the leakage inductance energy. Also, ZCS switching condition is established for the auxiliary switch moreover, due to most diodes ZCS turn-off, the reverse recovery problem is reduced. In this converter, the input voltage source and load have a common ground furthermore, the converter benefits from continuous input current. In this paper, the presented converter is analyzed completely and simulated at 200 W output power which 96.8% efficiency shows the converter high quality.

articleTitle: Optimizing Microgrid Energy Management: Metaheuristic versus Conventional Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Widespread deployment of renewable energy resources (RES) is presently taking place to satisfy the escalating energy demands, alleviate environmental pollution, and attain socioeconomic advantages that promote sustainable development. The feasibility of implementing microgrids (MG) is created by the integration of such distributed energy sources into the utility grid. The intermittent nature of RESs incorporated with MGs is, nevertheless, a result of their stochastic behavior. Thus, in order to guarantee a seamless transfer of MG power to sensitive loads and the primary grid, a suitable control strategy is indispensable. This paper undertakes an analysis of the application of meta-heuristic and conventional techniques in resolving various challenges related to distribution network Energy Management Systems (EMS) and MGs, following a thorough examination of MGs, their components, and varieties. In order to ensure that the reader comprehends the significance of these methods, the article provides a variety of case studies illustrating their application to a range of issues.

articleTitle: Peer-to-peer Energy Transaction Incorporating Prosumers’ Tendency with load and PV uncertainty consideration
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Residential microgrids consist of consumers and prosumers. In this microgrid consumers tend to reduce their energy costs. However, in microgrid that incorporates peer-to-peer capabilities, prosumers could have different objectives. In this way, prosumers can also increase their energy sales to consumers in addition to reducing their energy costs. Therefore, in the presented approach prosumers predetermined their energy sales to reduce their cost or increase their energy sales to the consumers. In this study, a hierarchical approach is presented to consider the energy transaction and prosumers’ objectives. Initially, the self-scheduling of prosumers to determined their transacted energy is presented. Subsequently, through the consideration of energy sharing, the maximization of societal welfare is pursued. Moreover, the sensitivity analysis is utilized to evaluate the effect of load and photovoltaic panel output power uncertainties on the obtained results. The proposed method is investigated in a test residential microgrid with 40 units, which includes 20 prosumers and 20 consumers. The simulation is conducted utilizing Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) within the GAMS, employing the CPLEX solver. According to the obtained results, by changing the load and output power of PVs, the benefit earned by prosumers changes. However, prosumers intending to reduce their costs have earned greater benefits than those aiming to increase their energy sales.

articleTitle: Microgrids: Characteristics and Emerging Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Microgrids have appeared as a feasible remedy for the energy sector and increase energy demand and climate change issues. These distributed energy networks combine local energy resources, advanced storage systems and intelligent management for independent work or communication with central networks. In this article, it is intended to examine the unique features and challenges of microgrids, highlight their flexibility in energy distribution, renewable integration, and a role in reducing greenhouse gas emissions. With the progress of microgrids, research and development are very important to advance energy systems to a sustainable future.

articleTitle: Optimal design of an off-grid multi-energy microgrid based on corona virus search optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper focuses on the optimal design of off-grid multi-energy microgrids (MEM). Optimizing such microgrids is paramount because they can provide sustainable and reliable energy solutions in remote or emergency scenarios. Thus, this study investigates the economic planning of an off-grid MEM composed of wind turbines (WT), photovoltaic (PV), electric vehicles (EV), batteries energy storage (BES), combined heat and power (CHP) systems, and thermal energy storage (TES). The optimization objective considered in this problem includes capital investment, maintenance, and operational costs. By modeling the operation of resources and storage system, priority is given to supplying electrical loads through wind turbines, solar panels, and combined heat and power systems. The electrical and thermal storage devices also play a role in matching supply and demand. This study employs the Corona Virus Search Optimizer (CVSO), an optimization algorithm inspired by virus behavior. The simulation results demonstrate the enhanced efficiency and performance of the CVSO algorithm in optimizing the design of off-grid multi-energy microgrid systems. Furthermore, this system’s optimal design has successfully provided electrical and thermal loads with minimized costs.

articleTitle: Cost-benefit Analysis of PV Self-Consumption in Residential Sector in Italy
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: For nearly ten years, residential photovoltaic (PV) system installation has increased dramatically, driven by national initiatives like Feed-in Tariffs and Net Metering. With the focus on maximizing system earnings, consumers are increasingly turning to enhancing self-consumption. Despite the exploration of various facets, there are still challenges impeding the full achievement of the utilization of these technologies. The substantial initial cost of purchasing a PV system includes expenses for solar panels, installations, inverters, and associated equipment. The research aims to evaluate the financial feasibility of household photovoltaic self-consumption for reducing consumers’ electricity bills. the study evaluates different solar panel capacities, ranging from 1 kWp to 4 kWp in Rome and Milan. To achieve this goal, the study compares a representative Italian home solely dependent on the electricity grid with a hypothetical scenario in which the residence engages in a PV self-production project to cover all or part of its energy needs. The assessment includes the hourly pricing of potential surplus energy sold to the grid, using a simplified compensation system for a period of one year starting January 1, 2023. The results show the profitability of PV self-consumption installations: Rome, a 1k W p PV system demonstrates commendable results $(P I=3.336)$, (IRR $=21 \%$), boasting the quickest payback time in four and half years and DPP in more than five years, also the highest NPV (€ 5126.786). Milan, a 1 kWp PV system achieves an impressive score $(\mathrm{PI}=3.147),(I R R={2 0 \%})$, accompanied by a short payback period of five years and DPP in five and half years, also the greatest NPV (€ 4712.598).

articleTitle: Electric Spring to Power Factor Correction and Voltage Regulation of PV System by Considering Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: abstract-With the increasing global demand for electrical energy and facing environmental challenges such as global warming and the depletion of fossil fuel resources, the importance of utilizing renewable energy sources has become significant. On the other hand, due to the stochastic nature of renewable energy sources, it is challenging to make the generated energy directly proportional to the consumption. This leads to variations in the network voltage. In this paper, Electric Springs (ES) is proposed as a demand response technology to enhance the stability and power quality of emerging power systems with a high penetration of intermittent renewable energy sources. In recent years, Electric Springs have been introduced as a tool for demand-side management in microgrids or networks with a substantial share of renewable energy. This equipment, acting as a controlled voltage source through a series connection with non-sensitive loads, introduces a smart load capable of altering current and consequently non-sensitive load power, thus balancing the fluctuations in renewable energy sources and load. In this article, an analytical method for controlling first and second-generation Electric Springs is presented to improve the power factor of the network and regulate the voltage of sensitive loads by modeling the effects of uncertainty and oscillations in renewable energy sources. The results indicate that the proposed method using secondgeneration Electric Springs can lead to an improvement in power factor and voltage regulation under conditions of over voltage or decrease.

articleTitle: Quadratic High Step-up DC-DC Converter With Passive Clamp Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: abstract-This paper presents a quadratic high step-up DCDC converter incorporating a coupled inductor (CI), a passive clamp circuit and a voltage multiplier cell (VMC). This converter operates based on parallel charging of capacitors by CI and series discharging of this energy at the output. Moreover, the converter includes a diode-capacitor clamp circuit to decrease the voltage stress on the active switch and the output diode. As a result, this converter has high voltage gain (VG) and low voltage stress on switches, which is appropriate to increase the output voltage in photovoltaic panels. Since the proposed converter reduces voltage stress on the active switch, a switch with low resistance is utilized, which is improving power efficiency. The presented converter is analyzed in continuous conduction mode (CCM), discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) and steady-state. The experimental results relevant to the presented converter is verified with a $300 \mathrm{~V}-90 \mathrm{~W}$ prototype.

articleTitle: Unveiling Mountaineering Team-Based Optimization Algorithm forPerformance Enhancement of Radial Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: The inadequate capacity of Radial Distribution Networks (RDNs) to accommodate renewable energy sources and the suboptimal allocation of Distributed Generation Sources (DGs) pose significant challenges. This paper introduces a cooperative approach utilizing meta-heuristic algorithms to address these challenges simultaneously through Distribution Network Reconfiguration (DNR) and the optimal allocation (i.e., siting and sizing) of DGs. Integrating these two tasks is a complex endeavor, particularly within a multi-objective framework. To tackle this complexity, a multi-objective function is formulated, aiming to minimize ohmic losses, enhance voltage profiles, and reduce DG costs while adhering to system constraints. Fuzzification techniques are employed to transform this multiobjective function into a single-objective problem, simplifying the optimization process. DNR, involving optimized changes to tielines between distribution system feeders without altering their radial structure, is modeled as a solution to facilitate the optimal DG allocation and cost reduction. This study focuses on renewable-based DGs, such as Wind Turbines (WTs). This paper introduces a robust algorithm called Mountaineering Team-Based Optimization (MTBO), for the first time, applied to the challenge of simultaneous network Reconfiguration and DGs optimal allocation. MTBO is mathematically formalized to provide a robust optimization approach inspired by social behavior and human cooperation. Experimental investigations encompass the simultaneous integration of DNR and DG optimal allocation, utilizing the 33-bus IEEE and 69-bus IEEE distribution test systems to demonstrate the method’s efficacy and superiority. Simulation results are compared under uncertain conditions, highlighting MTBO’s efficiency compared to alternative algorithms like the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The outcomes affirm the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method, indicating its effectiveness and robustness in comparison with competitive algorithms. The repositioning of optimal DG units significantly improves performance, quality, and reliability in RDNs, as evidenced by these simulations.

articleTitle: Increasing Social Contribution in Urban Energy Projects Using Process Improvement Methodologies
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: With importance of public participation in urban energy plans, this article aims to review new applications of Six Sigma methodology for urban energy management companies to increase public participation in demand response plans.

articleTitle: Microgrid Bidding Strategy with Uncertain Renewable Sources and Interruptible Loads in Energy and Spinning Reserve Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: A microgrid scheme typically consist of distributed generation sources along with controllable/interruptible loads in addition to storage facilities. The scheme is an effective paradigm to integrate dispatchable and non-dispatchable generation sources in the low voltage networks on the local scale. The increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energies in the markets has deteriorated the complexity of competitive market models due to uncertainties. In this paper, an optimal microgrid bidding strategy is introduced for participation in the day-ahead energy market and spinning reserve market. The strategy takes into account the uncertainty of wind and solar supply patterns, load variations, and energy price fluctuations in the electricity market. The proposed model of a microgrid sample was simulated using the GAMS software. A comparison was then conducted between the results of the proposed strategy and the deterministic bidding strategy approach to showcase the optimality and superiority of the former.

articleTitle: MPSO-Based Economic Optimal Design of an Isolated Industrial Microgrid Considering LPSP Concept and Covering System Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: This paper introduces a comprehensive long-term design and optimization approach for an isolated industrial microgrid comprising a wind turbine (WT), photovoltaic(PV) cells, a diesel generator and battery storage. The methodology takes into consideration the uncertainties associated with consumption load and the generation of distributed energy resources, employing a Monte Carlo scenario generation method. The optimal number of components for the hybrid system is determined by evaluating the Loss of Power Supply Probability (LPSP) using the proposed model. This evaluation is conducted through two conventional particle swarm algorithms (PSO) and Modified PSO (MPSO). The primary objective is to minimize the annual cost of the designed and analyzed system. The analysis reveals that the results demonstrate superior optimal performance and faster convergence speed of the proposed algorithm. The results demonstrate the optimal performance of the WT/PV/battery/diese hybrid system, with an annual system cost of 463,449.03 ${\$}$. Furthermore, as $L P S P_{\max }$ increases, the optimal annual cost of the system decreases, along with the number of batteries in all three investigated hybrid systems. Simultaneously, the share of diesel generator production increases.

articleTitle: Reliability and Lifetime Analysis of a Standalone PV System Employing Fuzzy Logic and P&O MPPT Methods Under Faulty Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In light of the increasing need for solar power, fueled by the depletion of fossil resources and their ecological consequence, various studies have been conducted to improve the tracking of the maximum power point. This optimization aims to enhance the utilization of PV cell power, especially in standalone applications, given the vital role of electricity in agriculture and local consumption. Hence, considerations regarding reliability and lifetime management hold substantial importance. This study delves into the examination and analysis of MPPT controllers, including the conventional P&O and Fuzzy Logic, for their application in PV systems. To achieve this objective, a 100 kW off-grid PV system is employed. Following the implementation of the two mentioned MPPT techniques, their critical failure modes undergo investigation through lifetime analysis. In order to assess the reliability status of these MPPTs under faulty conditions, appropriate reliability criteria are selected. The outcomes of the reliability assessments lead to the derivation of Markov chains, and the study on reliability provides the Mean Time to Failure as a metric for lifetime estimation. Additionally, their performance in the face of rapid load changes is employed to analyze the stability of each method. Ultimately, the most reliable MPPT method is recommended for standalone PV system, serving as a guide for engineering applications.

articleTitle: The impact of Energy Storage System on the flexible operation of the Renewable-Based Virtual Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: In the coming years, an adaptive power system is essential in order to incorporate the growing distributed generations (DGs) and renewable energy sources (RESs) with Energy Storage System (ESS) facilities. virtual power plant (VPP) represents a cutting-edge power generation technology that consolidates and optimizes generation, network constraints, energy storage devices, and demands. It offers significant improvements in power system flexibility, facilitates better utilization of distributed generations in the user-side, and fosters the progress of wholesale markets. Despite its potential, VPP is currently in its early stages of development. Current work imposes the VPP concept to implement proactive inspection over diverse DERs. The paper explores the impact of DERs on each other and climaxes the benefits of the VPP idea, Considering the technical, and economic features. Moreover, the model considers uncertainties associated with Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) via a scenario-driven probabilistic method. The framework is mathematically described as a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model, ensuring the optimal solution globally. To validate its effectiveness, the framework is utilized for the IEEE 33-BUS distribution test grid, and the results demonstrate VPP’s capability in controlling challenges such as power curtailment posed by RESs through ESS facilities.

articleTitle: Analyzing Consumer Behavior Insights from Smart Meter Data: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning and Traditional Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Therapid deployment of smart meters has transformed the utility sector, offering real-time, highresolution data for improved energy management, grid optimization, and customer engagement. Smart meters, including SMETS1 (Smart Metering Equipment Technical Specifications) and SMETS2 (the second and more advanced generation), record and communicate real-time consumption data, enabling quick detection of faults and irregularities for prompt maintenance. Analyzing the performance and preferences of different smart meter generations, along with non-smart meters, is crucial for optimizing deployment and understanding their impact on energy consumption behavior. This paper aimed to analyze consumer behavior insights from smart meter data through two distinct approaches: deep learning using a Sequential model and traditional machine learning employing Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and Random Forest algorithms. The dataset, containing information on Grid Supply Point (GSP), Primary location, and various numerical metrics, underwent a thorough preprocessing stage to handle missing values, normalize numerical features, and encode categorical variables. For the deep learning approach, a Sequential model was constructed with input and hidden layers, aiming to predict the number of smart meters (SMETS1 and SMETS2). The model achieved an accuracy of 61% and a loss of 0.02%, showcasing promising results. In the alternative approach, a classification task was formulated to predict whether a location has the highest number of smart meters (SMETS1 and SMETS2) or not. Logistic Regression outperformed Decision Tree and Random Forest models, achieving an accuracy of 98%.

articleTitle: Pitch Angle Control in Wind Turbines Using a Robust MRAC and σ Correction
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Wind energy is one of the most important renewable energysources. In modern wind turbines, two critical control levels exist, including pitch angle control and power converter control. Pitch angle control plays a significant role in determining the power output of the wind turbine, as well as maintaining the health of the blades and the overall structure of the turbine. Disturbances in variablespeed turbines can lead to inefficiencies in classical control methods. This paper utilizes a Model Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC) approach, but its performance becomes unstable under certain operating conditions. To enhance the robustness of MRAC, σ correction is employed as Robust Model Reference Adaptive Control (RMRAC). The proof stability of proposed strategy is done in this paper. The methods used in this study are evaluated based on real data from a 2.5 MW MAPNA wind turbine. The results of the designed controller based on adaptive reference model control demonstrate improved performance compared to classical control and adaptive reference model control alone, showcasing better adaptability to changes and resistance to disturbances. Pitch angle control in wind turbines using robust adaptive reference model control achieves desired power and rotational speed with minimal changes.

articleTitle: Analyzing Electrical Centrality Metrics for Optimal Placement of Microgrids and Renewable Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Thegoal of this paper is to explore the effect of centrality metrics in complex power networks, focusing specifically on their applications in the analysis of power grids. Through an in-depth survey, the study delves into the realm of structural and operational centrality measures, shedding light on their crucial role in understanding the structure and operational dynamics of power systems. The research highlights the significance of shortest path-based centrality measures, i.e., closeness and betweenness, in power grid analysis, including original, structural, and operational metrics. Simulation results from IEEE test cases reveal key insights regarding the similarities between structural and operational measures, the impact of electrical distances on node positioning, and variations in closeness metrics compared to betweenness. Observations related to operational measures show the pronounced shifts in closeness under varied operating conditions and the minimal influence of demand and generation changes on betweenness. Furthermore, the study extends previous research to optimize the placement of microgrids and renewable sources using complex network analysis, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed methodology in identifying critical nodes in power grids during outage scenarios.

articleTitle: Rooftop Photovoltaics Hosting Capacity Enhancement of Urban Distribution Networks Using Water Storage in Tall Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Moving toward renewables is a growing global trend mainly due to energy security issues and environmental concerns. However, technical issues such as buses voltages and lines flows restrict the integration of renewables into power grids at high levels of penetration. Thus, the Hosting Capacity (HC) of distribution networks for renewables must be evaluated and enhanced using available potentials. One of the main applicable types of renewables in urban areas is rooftop Photovoltaic (PVs). On the other hand, urban areas mainly consist of numerous tall buildings that require water for residents. In this paper, the potential of elevated water storage for supplying building’s water needs is investigated in order to enhance the HC of rooftop PVs in an urban distribution network. Therefore, the available roof area of tall buildings is utilized to install water tanks and PV systems. The optimization results (96 -hour horizon of 4 selected days) of the proposed model for the IEEE 33-bus network demonstrate the effectiveness of using the aforementioned potential to increase the HC of the network for renewable integration.

articleTitle: An Interleaved Bidirectional Switched-Capacitor Converter with Reduced Stress on the Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Switched-capacitor converters offer high efficiency and power density however, the technique is entangled with large transient currents, transferred between capacitors which relegate the application to lower powers. To this end, a variety of solutions have been presented in the literature. In this paper an interleaved bidirectional topology is proposed based on preceding works offering a reduced stress on the capacitors. Also, the gain of voltage and switch voltage stresses are respectively twice and half the bidirectional boost. The test has been performed on a hybrid electric vehicle. The results suggest a more sluggish response but less current ripple compared to the boost. Also, it presents a more superior performance in contrast to the akin switched capacitor topology. As such, it will be suitable for higher power applications.

articleTitle: Triphenylamine and Carbazol as Hole Transport Materials in Solid-State Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 11th Iranian Conference on Renewable Energy and Distribution Generation (ICREDG)
abstract: Significant attention is directed towards advancing dyesensitized solar cells (DSSCs). DSSCs comprise a complex assembly of components, each playing a critical role in facilitating efficient energy conversion. Of particular significance are the hole transport materials (HTMs), which serve as integral components responsible for transporting positive charges within the cell. HTMs encompass various classes of materials, in the meantime small organic compounds have emerged as the forefront contenders for facilitating charge transport in Solid-state dye-synthesized solar cells (ssDSCs). triphenylamine and carbazol emerge as a prominent candidate, owing to its unique chemical structure and inherent electrondonating properties. Triphenylamine exhibits a pronounced capacity for donating electrons, primarily attributed to the lone pair of nitrogen atoms and the arrangement of three phenyl rings within its molecular framework. This structural configuration facilitates efficient charge transfer mechanisms within the solar cell, consequently enhancing the stability and performance of solid-state dye-sensitized solar cells.
